ROUTER_PROMPT = (
    "You are a hybrid router for MMLU-Pro computer science multiple-choice questions. "
    "Your job is to select exactly one model—nano or mini—to answer each question, optimizing for both cost and accuracy. "
    "The router must stay on the Pareto frontier: always select the cheapest model likely to answer correctly, and escalate to mini only when nano is likely to fail but mini is likely to succeed. "
    "Critical misroutes—where nano is selected but is wrong while mini would be correct—are strongly penalized and must be avoided.\n\n"
    "**Domain and Task Details:**\n"
    "- The questions are from the computer science domain, including topics such as algorithms, data structures, computer architecture, networking, distributed systems, logic, and programming languages.\n"
    "- nano is a cheaper, less capable model; mini is more expensive but more accurate, especially on complex or subtle questions.\n"
    "- The router may use deterministic Python code to handle only the most obvious easy cases (see below), but all other cases must be routed to a model (nano or mini) by following the routing policy.\n\n"
    "**Routing Policy:**\n"
    "1. **Default to nano** for:\n"
    "   - Short, straightforward definitions, standard facts, abbreviation expansions, and simple code tracing (e.g. a tiny loop or what a variable equals after assignment, with no tricky logic).\n"
    "   - Very short questions with clear 'what is', 'define', or 'stands for' patterns and no hard markers.\n"
    "2. **Escalate to mini** for questions involving:\n"
    "   - Negations or ambiguity: 'NOT', 'EXCEPT', 'None of the above', 'Not enough information' (including similar phrases).\n"
    "   - 'Which of the following' patterns (these often require subtle reasoning or multi-statement evaluation).\n"
    "   - Roman numerals (I., II., III.), multi-statement choices, or logical operators (and/or/not, implication, etc).\n"
    "   - Multi-step calculations, subtle formal logic, advanced topics: cache simulation, matrix/rank, unification, recursion, entropy, Bayesian/probability reasoning, graph algorithms (vertex cover, clique, flow), distributed systems (chord, DHT), networking tools (nmap), or protocol/architecture edge cases.\n"
    "   - Any question where neither model is likely to answer correctly (to avoid under-escalation).\n"
    "3. **If both models are likely to answer correctly, always choose nano** to save cost.\n"
    "4. **If neither model is likely to answer correctly, choose mini** to avoid under-escalating difficult, failure-prone cases.\n"
    "5. **Deterministic Python code** may only handle the most obvious easy cases (see below); all other cases must be routed to the model router.\n\n"
    "**Examples:**\n"
    "- 'What is the definition of a stack?' → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following is a property of a binary search tree?' → nano\n"
    "- 'What is the output of this simple loop?' → nano\n"
    "- 'What does CPU stand for?' → nano\n"
    "- 'Which of the following expressions is true if X but not Y?' (with logical conditions and/or Roman numerals) → mini\n"
    "- 'Cache simulation, matrix rank, unification, protocol edge case, or ambiguous NOT/EXCEPT wording' → mini\n\n"
    "**Python Easy Router Function:**\n"
    "- The function route_easy_case(question, options, category=\"\", source=\"\") must return only 'nano', 'mini', or 'defer'.\n"
    "- It may only return 'nano' for very short, obvious definition/abbreviation questions with no hard markers (see below).\n"
    "- It must return 'defer' for all other cases, including any question with:\n"
    "  - Negations ('not', 'except', 'none of the above', 'not enough information')\n"
    "  - 'Which of the following' (as these often require subtle reasoning)\n"
    "  - Roman numerals ('I.', 'II.', 'III.')\n"
    "  - Advanced topics or markers: 'cache', 'matrix', 'rank', 'unification', 'boolean', 'recurs', 'capacity', 'entropy', 'half-life', 'bayesian', 'vertex cover', 'maximum clique', 'maximum flow', 'chord', 'dht', 'nmap', 'probability', 'expectation', 'random variable', 'distribution', 'graph', 'tree', 'edge case', 'protocol', 'memory', 'pointer', 'stack overflow', 'deadlock', 'race condition', 'critical section'\n"

def route_easy_case(question, options, category="", source=""):
    """Return 'nano' for obvious easy cases; return 'defer' for the model router."""
    text = (question + "\n" + "\n".join(options)).lower()

    # Expanded and reorganized hard markers for better coverage and early exit on any hard topic
    hard_markers = [
        "not", "except", "none of the above", "not enough information",
        "which of the following", "i.", "ii.", "iii.",
        "cache", "matrix", "rank", "unification", "boolean", "recurs", "recursion",
        "capacity", "entropy", "half-life", "bayesian", "vertex cover",
        "maximum clique", "maximum flow", "chord", "dht", "nmap",
        "probability", "expectation", "random variable", "distribution",
        "graph", "tree", "edge case", "protocol", "memory", "pointer",
        "stack overflow", "deadlock", "race condition", "critical section"
    ]
    for marker in hard_markers:
        if marker in text:
            return "defer"

    # Only consider nano for short, clear, definition/abbreviation/simple code trace
    easy_markers = [
        "what is", "what are", "define", "definition", "stands for",
        "abbreviation", "expands to", "meaning of", "refers to", "is defined as",
        "in computer science, what", "means", "describes", "purpose of", "role of",
        "simple loop", "repeat", "standard fact"
    ]

    # Additional strictness: require question to be short and not have any numbers (to avoid code tracing with numbers or subtle logic)
    if len(question) < 130:
        for marker in easy_markers:
            if marker in question.lower():
                # Safeguard: avoid 'nano' if any option contains a hard marker (e.g. "none of the above" as an option)
                for m in hard_markers:
                    for o in options:
                        if m in o.lower():
                            return "defer"
                return "nano"

    return "defer"
# EVOLVE-BLOCK-END

    return ROUTER_PROMPT
